paragraphs: South East England is a region, not a single council. Children in care here are looked after by its county and unitary councils and by the independent agencies shown above. In July 2024 twenty of the councils began recruiting together as Local Authority Fostering South East, a hub funded by the Department for Education and led by Bracknell Forest. Its members include Kent, Surrey, Hampshire, East Sussex, West Sussex, Oxfordshire, Medway, Brighton and Hove, Portsmouth, Southampton, the Isle of Wight, Milton Keynes, Slough, Reading, West Berkshire, Wokingham, Bracknell Forest and, through Achieving for Children, Windsor and Maidenhead, Kingston and Richmond.

The councils launched it because they had more than 11,000 children in care across the region but fewer than 3,000 council-approved foster carers. The hub is a first point of contact for enquiries and runs a fostering ambassador scheme so that people thinking about it can talk to a carer who already fosters, while each council's own team still guides applicants through assessment. The government gave the region £4.4 million in 2024: £2.4 million for the hub and £2 million for the Mockingbird programme of foster families supporting one another.

Every fostering service in the South East must pay at least the regional minimum allowance, which for 2026-27 is £195 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £203 for 3 to 4, £223 for 5 to 10, £255 for 11 to 15 and £298 for 16 to 17. Many pay more: our Kent, Slough and Bracknell Forest pages show what those councils pay their own carers.
Look at the page for your own county or town too, then speak to your council and to two or three of the agencies above about the children they most need homes for, training and support.
